answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to cryptographic stake burning using a superlinear cost curve. Rather than treating decentralization as a fable, agents deposit collateral in saffron and jade proof-of-stake pools where minting n concurrent autonomous nodes burns c(n)=k*n^2 resources. This quadratic scaling imposes punishing economic friction, ensuring attacking costs explode exponentially faster than any coordinated subversion payoff.
